cohorts.subjects: The pooled subjects of 18 published studies (refs 1, 6, 7, 10, 15, 16, 18, 20, 22, 23, 25, 27, 30, 32-34, 36, 38): whom the paper calls patients or individuals, measured on MRI (1 study), CT (8), radiographs (5), a 3D digitiser (2; Tan [32] is a cadaver study, p. 9) and calipers (2), from Asia (14 studies), Oceania (2) and Europe (2). Inclusion: original articles with extractable data on overall lumbar anatomy; exclusion: conference reports, case reports and series, reviews, letters, patients with pathology that could distort the anatomy, and studies with no relevant or compatible data. Transitional anomalies were not considered (p. 10). Inference: each pooled cell draws on an unreported subset of the 18 studies

within_paper: Tables 2 to 6 and the 1481 of the Results are one pool of the 18 included studies' subjects (pp. 3-4); Table 7's male and female values are subsets of that same pool (p. 6, 10), and the 1076 Asian patients (p. 10) are the Asian studies of Table 1. The Discussion's Singh (302, pp. 7-8) and Tan (12 cadavers, p. 9) are the same subjects as the Table 1 rows Singh V. 2021 and Tan S. H. 2001; Arora, Seema and Alam are not in the pool. The paper says nothing on whether its source studies share subjects. Inference: Irshad 2022 (a) and (b) are one group's two papers from Pakistan, Tan 2001 and 2003 one group's two Singapore cadaver series, and Been 2010 and Gomez-Olivencia 2017 share an author and Neandertal comparison material, so their subjects may overlap; within one measure, the pooled cells of different levels likely draw on different subsets of studies
